latest_release.body:
**Antigravity Google login, scriptable API-key setup, and always-on Jarvis voice**

### Highlights

- Google personal accounts now sign in through Antigravity with Gemini 4 (Neon) as the default model and pooled Gemini, Argon, and Claude quota bars in the account router.
- Every API-key provider now supports non-interactive login with --api-key, --api-key-env, and --json, including scripted AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI setup.
- Always-on Jarvis voice now streams live captions as you speak, recovers automatically after network outages, and keeps a session-only replay history of accepted requests.

### Improvements

- Model and fuzzy pickers now rank literal substring matches ahead of typo and usage-boosted loose matches.
- Todo lists now support withdrawing tasks by name with archived reasons while keeping retired and delegated work out of active reminders.
- Queued follow-up messages now preserve image attachments and are delivered before retrying empty post-tool answers.
- Long-running background tasks now trigger a one-time review after five minutes, while routine swarm wait receipts stay hidden from the transcript.
- macOS menu bar session counts now render with native contrast, including 0/0 when idle.

### Fixes

- Reading a 13th screenshot no longer drops earlier images or invalidates the prompt cache just because of image count (retains tool images up to 48 MiB).
- Retired Gemini Code Assist personal OAuth entries are hidden from login pickers and routed to Antigravity instead.
- Jarvis speech playback waits until the microphone is quiet and keeps live captions, provisional turns, and final transcripts ordered per utterance.
- Coordinator interrupts in swarms now stay scoped to the addressed session rather than interrupting unrelated workers.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/compare/v1.0.1...v1.0.3

# jcode

High-performance coding agents.
Run dozens of agents in parallel without melting your machine. More agents, less RAM, no lag.

## Installation
```bash # macOS & Linux curl -fsSL https://jcode.sh/install | bash ``` Want to switch to prereleases (Linux x86_64) and live-update running sessions? Run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://jcode.sh/install | bash -s -- --prerelease ``` Already on a recent build? You can also run `jcode update --prerelease` (or `/update prerelease` inside jcode), and switch back anytime with `jcode update --stable` (or `/update stable`). See [Update channels](docs/UPDATE_CHANNELS.md) and [Linux self-dev prereleases](RELEASING.md#linux-self-dev-prereleases).
## Benches

## Swarm Spawn two or more agents in the same repo, and they will automatically be managed by the server to allow native collaboration. When agent A edits a file that agent B has read (code shifting under its feet), the server notifies agent B. Agent B can ignore it if it is not relevant, or it can check the diff to make sure that it doesn't conflict. Each agent has messaging abilities, capable of DMing just one agent, broadcasting to all other agents hosted by the server, or just agents working in that repo. This allows you to spawn multiple sessions in the same repo, and have all conflicts automatically resolved. Agents are also able to spawn their own swarms autonomously. They have a swarm tool which allows them to spawn in their own teamates to accomplish tasks in parallel. Doing so turns the main agent into a coordinator and the spawned agents into workers. Groups of agents, their messaging channels, their completion statuses, etc are all automatically managed. This can be done headlessly or headed. ## OAuth and Providers Supports a [wide range of providers](https://jcode.sh/docs#providers), including Claude OAuth and OpenAI Codex OAuth. ## Customizability / Self-Dev Jcode is inventing a new form of customizability. One that doesn't limit you to what a plugin or extension can do. Tell your jcode agent to enter self dev mode, and it will start modifying its own source code. Jcode is optimized to iterate on itself. There is significant infrastructure around self development, which allows it to edit, build, and test its own source code, then reload its own binary and continue work in your (potentially many) sessions, fully automatically. ## Other - [Token optimization](docs/HARNESS.md#token-optimization) - [KV cache](docs/HARNESS.md#kv-cache) - [Hill-climbable measurements](docs/HARNESS.md#hill-climbable-measurements)
